seoTitle: How to Close a Google Workspace Account in 2026
metaDescription: Close a Google Workspace account properly — export your data, cancel the subscription, clear Marketplace apps, and delete the organisation before the next bill.
intro: Closing a Google Workspace account is not one button, and that surprises people who assume cancelling the subscription is the end of it. Google separates the two deliberately: cancelling stops the billing, while deleting the organisation removes the users, the data, and the domain association — and it will not let you do the second until the first has finished. There is also a waiting period built in, because Google starts deleting your data the moment you cancel and won't close the account until that finishes. That timing is the whole reason to start this at least a week before your renewal date rather than the night before. This guide walks the full sequence in the order the Admin console actually enforces, with the two irreversible moments flagged clearly.

steps.heading: Sign in with a super admin account
steps.body: Go to admin.google.com and choose the right account — this is the step that trips people up, because a personal Gmail address cannot administer a Workspace organisation. Google says so directly on the sign-in page: you need an administrator account for a managed Google service. If the account picker shows several identities, pick the one on your Workspace domain, not the gmail.com one. You also need super admin rights specifically; a delegated admin with billing access can cancel a subscription but cannot delete the organisation, and you'll only discover that halfway through.

image.caption: The admin.google.com sign-in, noting that an administrator account is required and listing the signed-in identities to choose from.

steps.heading: Find your way around the Admin console
steps.body: The console home shows a Manage Workspace panel with Users and Billing cards side by side, and the Billing card tells you when your paid service starts or renews. Note that date now — it's your deadline. Everything in this process lives in two places on the left-hand menu: Billing, which holds Subscriptions and Payment accounts, and Account, which holds Account settings. Expand both before you go any further so you can move between them without hunting. If Billing shows a trial rather than a paid subscription, the same sequence applies; a trial that isn't cancelled converts to a paid plan on the date shown.

image.caption: The Admin console home, with the Billing card showing the paid service start date and the Account section expanded in the left menu.

steps.heading: Export everything you want to keep — first
steps.body: Do this before you cancel anything, because cancellation starts the clock on data deletion. Use the data export tool in Account settings to pull mail, Drive files, contacts, and calendars for every user in the organisation, and remember it can take days to produce the archive for a large account. If a single user's mailbox is what matters, Google Takeout for that account is faster. Also transfer ownership of any shared Drive files to an account you're keeping, since files owned by a deleted user disappear even if other people could see them. Once the export lands, open it and confirm it contains what you expect rather than trusting the completion email.

steps.heading: Open Account settings and find Account management
steps.body: In the left menu, go to Account, then Account settings. Scroll past the personalisation and smart-features panels to the Account management section — it's an unremarkable collapsed row that carries the plainest warning in the whole console: deleting the account will permanently delete all user accounts, their data, and their access to services. Expand it. This section is the actual closure workflow, and it presents itself as a numbered checklist of things Google requires you to finish before the delete button becomes usable.

image.caption: Account settings scrolled to the Account management row, warning that deletion permanently removes all user accounts and their data.

steps.heading: Clear the required blockers
steps.body: The checklist marks each unfinished item with a red icon and refuses to let you proceed until they're green. Two are near-universal: cancelling your organisation's active subscriptions, and uninstalling any Marketplace apps. Google spells out the consequence in the subscription item — cancelling starts deleting your organisation's data, and you have to wait for that deletion to finish before the account itself can be removed. Each item gives you a direct link through to where it's handled, so use "Go to Subscriptions" and "Uninstall installed Marketplace apps" rather than navigating there yourself and losing your place in the list. There's also an export-other-Google-data prompt above the checklist, which is your last reminder if you skipped the previous step.

image.caption: The account management checklist, flagging active subscriptions and installed Marketplace apps as required steps with direct links to each.

steps.heading: Cancel the subscription itself
steps.body: Under Billing, Subscriptions lists every plan on the account with its status, licence count, payment plan, and when payment is due — and there is often more than one row, since archived-user storage and add-ons bill separately from the main plan. Cancel each of them, not just the headline subscription, or the account will keep a live plan and refuse to close. Watch the payment-due column as you go: a plan showing paid service starting in a few days is one you want cancelled today. Save or screenshot the cancellation confirmation for each, because that is your evidence if a charge appears later.

steps.heading: Delete the account and confirm nothing is left
steps.body: Once the checklist is clear and Google's data deletion has run its course, return to Account management and complete the deletion. This is irreversible: the users, their mail, and their files are gone, and the account cannot be restored afterwards. Before you press it, check three things — that your domain's MX records are pointed somewhere else if you still own the domain, that any third-party services using Workspace as a single sign-on have been migrated, and that no automatic payment remains active on the payment account. Then watch your card statement through the date you noted at the start; a closed account should produce no further charge on the next cycle.

faq.question: Is cancelling my subscription the same as closing the account?
faq.answer: No. Cancelling stops the billing; closing the account deletes the organisation, its users, and their data. Google requires the cancellation first and won't let you delete the account until the resulting data deletion has finished.

faq.question: Why won't the Admin console let me delete my account?
faq.answer: Something on the required checklist is still outstanding — most often an active subscription or an installed Marketplace app. Both are flagged in Account management with direct links to resolve them.

faq.question: Will I be charged again after I cancel?
faq.answer: Not if the cancellation completes before the payment-due date shown against each subscription. Cancel every subscription row, not just the main plan, and keep the confirmations in case a charge appears anyway.

faq.question: Can I get my data back after closing the account?
faq.answer: Assume not. The console states plainly that deletion permanently removes all user accounts, their data, and their access to services, so run a full data export and transfer ownership of shared files before you start.

faq.question: Do I need to be a super admin to do this?
faq.answer: Yes. A delegated admin with billing rights can cancel subscriptions but cannot delete the organisation. Sign in with a super admin account on the Workspace domain — a personal Gmail address cannot administer the organisation at all.
